core_meaning.short_meaning: Tender youth; companion al-Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi (Dhu al-Nur).
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Tufayl (طُفَيْل) is an authentic Arabic masculine name meaning 'tender, delicate youth' or 'gentle dawn'. In Islamic tradition, it belongs to al-Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi, the revered companion known as 'Dhu al-Nur' (Possessor of the Light), whose illuminated staff guided his people to Islam.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive form of ṭifl, meaning 'young and tender', expressing affectionate nobility and vitality.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root ṭ-f-l in classical lexicons signifies gentleness, tenderness, and dawn. In Islamic history, al-Tufayl ibn Amr was an eloquent chief of the Daws tribe who accepted Islam in Mecca despite tribal opposition. The Prophet ﷺ prayed for a sign for him, and a brilliant light shone from his whip, causing his tribe, including Abu Hurairah, to embrace the faith.
